mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the federal funds rate increases by more than 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where HOUST increases for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% over three months signals an improving labor market, which typically leads to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5% over three months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over three months signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which is a positive signal for corporate earnings and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO increases by more than 1% over three months.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) over three months, it signals strong consumer demand, which is a positive indicator for S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > CPIAUCSL growth in 3 months
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS growth exceeds CPIAUCSL growth over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over a month, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3%, signals a robust labor market and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k & UNRATE decrease > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.3% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over three consecutive months signals an easing monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as liquidity increases and borrowing costs decrease.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where FEDFUNDS decreases for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year growth rate of real GDP (GDPC1) exceeds the growth rate of the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 1%, it signals strong economic growth relative to inflation, which is a positive indicator for S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth > CPIAUCSL YoY growth + 1%
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where GDPC1 YoY growth exceeds CPIAUCSL YoY growth by more than 1%.
